messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify deleteNode correctly removes a node with only a left child and returns the left child as the new subtree root.
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures the function handles the case where the node to be deleted has only a left child, which is a key BST deletion scenario and a common source of pointer errors.

primary.name: deleteNode
primary.signature: struct node* deleteNode(struct node* root, int key)

dependencies.name: minValueNode
dependencies.reason: Required for other delete cases, not called in this path
dependencies.call_path: deleteNode → minValueNode (not taken in this path)

assertions.name: helper_assert_tree_inorder
assertions.purpose: Verify the inorder traversal of the resulting tree matches expected values

assertions.name: helper_assert_node_count
assertions.purpose: Verify the number of nodes in the tree is as expected after deletion

utilities.name: helper_build_tree
utilities.purpose: Builds a BST from an array of values for test setup
utilities.usage: Setup phase to create initial tree

utilities.name: helper_free_tree
utilities.purpose: Frees all nodes in the tree after test

preconditions: BST contains a node with only a left child
setup_requirements.initial_state: A BST with root node 10, left child 5, and no right child (10->left=5, 10->right=NULL)

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Pointer to root of BST with node 10 (left child 5, no right child)
primary_function_args.rationale: Ensures root node has only a left child, triggers the path

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Key of node to delete (root node, 10)
primary_function_args.rationale: Deletes the node with only a left child

return_value.description: Pointer to the left child (node 5), which becomes the new root
return_value.validation: Returned pointer is not NULL and points to node with key 5

side_effects.effect: Node with key 10 is freed and removed from the tree

state_changes: BST with nodes 10,5 → BST with only node 5
invariants_maintained: No memory leaks (all nodes freed at end)

assertions_required.description: Returned root is the left child (key 5)
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Returned pointer is not the expected left child

assertions_required.description: Tree contains only one node after deletion
Inorder traversal matches expected single-node tree

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All dynamically allocated nodes freed; no memory leaks

edge_cases_to_note: If left child has its own children, they must be preserved (not present in this minimal case)
No right child for deleted node

path_coverage_analysis.description: Delete node with only left child: free node, return left child as new root

integration_test_suggestions: Test deleting a node with only a left child when the left child itself has children (to ensure subtree is preserved).
Test deleting a node with only a right child (mirror of this path).
